title: The agent-monitor object of the access log, the record code of a read, the field list of an entry and the migration step are named in no source
source: Work Package _work/msr/wp/B2-P4-022.md (story line RWB-P4-E2031-APP, patterns DP03, DP07, DP10, DP13, DP15, DP19); _work/msr/context/P4.md (four provided REST operations, five tables, JOB-18, no event, no workflow); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md Appendix T-A.1 (API-P4-008 GET /admin/access-log with no parameter list; API-P4-012 GET /me/session); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md A2.7, A2.8 and A2.16
description: This slice records the agent-monitor reads on the access log of rwb-access and answers them back. Six values that the record and the read need are in no source: the object-type code of the agent monitor and the list it belongs to; the record code the local decision-record library gives an access event of a read; the field list of an access entry beyond the screen, the agent codes, the segment, the date range, the caller, the outcome and the time that this story states; the page bounds of the log read; the name of the read index on the record table; and the accept date and version number of the one Flyway step of DP-15. The two operations used are already published and carry no filter set in the TSD, so the object set is an addition this story has to fix and record rather than copy.
evidence: Context pack P4 lists exactly four provided operations and no filter or object set, five tables (delegation_limit, masking_rule, permission, role, role_conflict) and no access-entry table; TSD P4 v3 T-A.1 gives API-P4-008 as GET /admin/access-log with Platform administration R and no query row, and API-P4-012 as GET /me/session with no field list; FSD P4 v3 A2.7 and A2.8 describe the event and its decision-log linkage in prose with no field catalogue and no object type, and A2.16 describes the audit query with no parameter table; no read source names a record code for an access entry, a page bound, an index name or a migration version
owner_role: Tech lead of rwb-access with the ledger owner
proposed: Fix the object-type value on the access-log list in force and add it to the next version of the access-log contract of RWB-P4-E1039-CON; take the record code from the DP-03 library's code set at build time and state it in the contract; publish the entry field list and the page bounds with the log read; name the read index in the physical schema of rwb_access; and record the Flyway step in the service's own sequence. Every one of the six is a line in one contract document, not a schema change and not a business value.

title: The four platform contracts and the reference-data contract that the DP table adds are absent from the Work Package dependency lists
source: Work Package _work/msr/wp/B2-P4-022.md (story line RWB-P4-E2031-APP: H = [], C = [RWB-P10-E2031-CON], I = [], X = [], patterns DP03, DP07, DP10, DP13, DP15, DP19); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md R5.5 (the dependency column of DP-03, DP-07, DP-15 and DP-19) and R5.7 rule 3; _work/msr/context/P4.md
section: RWB-P4-E2031-APP metadata rows 15 to 18, and sections 3, 12.2, 13 and 19
description: The DP rows the Work Package claims add one build dependency each: DP-03 adds H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, DP-07 adds H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and C RWB-P3-E1043-CON, DP-15 adds H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON and DP-19 adds H RWB-PLT-N001-CON. The Work Package H list is empty and its C list holds RWB-P10-E2031-CON only, so a story that writes the local record, reads the lists in force, adds a Flyway step and is served through the composite route has five prerequisites that its rows do not carry. The rows are copied exactly as the Work Package fixes them and the five are stated in the story text instead; the C row RWB-P3-E1043-CON is the one that changes a build (the lists are read from Day 1), so it is the one that must be added before the story can be called Done.
evidence: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 dependency column: DP-03 'H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON', DP-07 'H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON', DP-15 'H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON', DP-19 'H RWB-PLT-N001-CON'; the Work Package line for RWB-P4-E2031-APP as quoted; context pack P4 confirms this service has no CON of its own in this Work Package and four provided operations that predate it
proposed: Add the five rows to the dependency map of the story set at D1: the four platform contracts to H and RWB-P3-E1043-CON to C. Keep the metadata of this Work Package unchanged and let the dependency map and the Build Sequence carry the correction, so that a parallel edit of the plan does not reopen the story file.

title: The legacy story and the rwb-agent contract name different rights for the same read of the agent monitor
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5/RWB E2 031 Agent monitoring dashboard v2 E3d v1.md (precondition 'The user holds Platform administration R'; section 10 and exception X6 with MSG-P4-002); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/RWB-SVC-P10 rwb-agent (Agent)/RWB P10 E2031 APP Agent monitoring dashboard v2 [E3d] v1.md section 12.1 (Rules and parameters R per TSD P10 API-P10-009, with the legacy Platform administration R recorded as ASM-B2-P10-005-12); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md T6.1
description: One read of SCR-46 now passes two gates: the screen route asks rwb-access whether the caller holds Platform administration R, as the legacy story fixes, and the metric read asks rwb-agent whether the caller holds Rules and parameters R, as the agent contract fixes. A role that holds one letter and not the other opens the screen and is then refused by the metric read, which is a 403 on a screen that looked open. No source states which of the two is the right of the agent monitor in the target, and the role matrix of TSD P4 T6.1 is published for three capability areas only, so the answer cannot be read from it either.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-031 precondition and section 10 name Platform administration R for the six roles and name RW-RISK as a receiver of alerts without that right; the delivered rwb-agent slice declares Rules and parameters R for GET /admin/agent-metrics and records the legacy right as ASM-B2-P10-005-12; TSD P4 v3 T6.1 gives RW-COE and the administrative roles R in Platform administration and gives no letter of Rules and parameters to RW-DATASTEW or RW-SECADM; FSD P4 v3 A2.30 title 'Control access by role and by agent' shows the administrative right carried in the access area
proposed: Keep both gates as they stand and treat the screen route's Platform administration R as the door of the screen and the metric read's Rules and parameters R as the right of the measure, and record in the access-review run of wave 2 which roles hold both. If the security administrator decides that one right must govern both, it is one permission row per role in the matrix in force and no code change in either story.

title: The secondary slice carries no legacy acceptance criterion of its own, and the legacy data, endpoint, job and screen blocks belong to other services and other slices
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5/RWB E2 031 Agent monitoring dashboard v2 E3d v1.md (sections 11, 12, 13 and 15: agent_run, agent_policy, agent_alert, agent_feedback, decision_log_entry, GET /api/recovery/v1/admin/agent-metrics, JOB-15, SCR-46); _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (RWB-E2-031 slices: RWB-P10-E2031-CON, -APP, RWB-P4-E2031-APP, RWB-P10-E2031-OPS, RWB-ITG-E2031-ITG, acs = []); _work/msr/context/P4.md (five tables, four operations)
description: The plan gives this slice no legacy acceptance criterion (acs is empty) and the legacy story has one access criterion only, exception X6, which is carried here as a new criterion in the Work Package's own words. Everything else in the legacy key — the metric endpoint, the segment filter, the drift check, the reconciliation, the agent tables and the screen content — is the rwb-agent slice's. This story therefore states its boundary in section 1, keeps the eight legacy test case ids for traceability only, and proves the authority answer and the record of the same read rather than restating a measure or a drift rule it does not own.
evidence: split_plan.json entry for RWB-P4-E2031-APP: acs [], tcs_legacy eight ids, secondary true; legacy section 12 declares GET /api/recovery/v1/admin/agent-metrics and JOB-15 and section 11 declares five agent tables and decision_log_entry, none of which this service owns; context pack P4 gives rwb-access five tables and four operations, none of them an agent table or a metric read; the delivered RWB-P10-E2031-APP declares the metric read, the drill-down, the drift activity and the reconciliation as its own
owner_role: Business analyst with the solution architect
proposed: Read the legacy key as two halves: the measures and the drift on rwb-agent, the authority and the record on rwb-access. At D1, confirm in the Story Catalog that the eight legacy test case ids are held by both slices, that no measure is implemented twice, and that exception X6 is the one access criterion the legacy story carries; no change is made to the legacy master in this run.
